name: Maasin Cathedral
description: Cathedral of Nuestra Senora de la Asuncion on the National Road, the largest and oldest church in the city (17th-century origins, current building completed 1968, seat of the Diocese of Maasin). Open mainly around mass; there is mass daily at 11 am.

name: Monte Cueva Shrine
address: Brgy. Rizal, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Chapel built inside a cave in Barangay Rizal (Sitio Basak), about 2 km from the city center; pilgrims climb about 550 concrete steps. A 30 ft statue of Our Lady of the Assumption stands above the Via Crucis. Official name: Shrine of the Most Precious Blood.

name: Camp Danao Forest Park
address: Brgy. Malapoc Sur, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: 320-hectare forest park about 15 km from Maasin proper at roughly 1,099 ft elevation, former Maasin City Forest Park and Boy Scouts jamboree site, with a lagoon, cave, trails, 360-degree viewing deck and camp area.

name: Guinsohotan Cave and Falls
description: Large subterranean cave about 15 km from the city center at around 276 m elevation. Wade or swim in to find small in-cave falls, bats and stalactite formations; the water flows out in cascades into a natural lagoon for bathing and picnics. Listed with Cagnituan Falls.

name: Cagnito-an Falls
address: Brgy. Cagnituan, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Cagnituan (Guinsohotan) Falls has its own underground river in a small forest; following it leads to Guinsohotan Cave. Reach it by multicab to Brgy. Maria Clara, then a habal-habal to Cagnituan.

name: Bogo Bird Paradise
description: Bird-watching spot listed under things to see in Maasin.
note: Only one source and no detail found; verify it is open.

name: Busay Falls
address: Brgy. Combado, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: One of Maasin City's waterfalls, in Barangay Combado, popular for swimming and picnics.
note: Trip101 places it in Brgy. Combado, Maasin. A Pintuyan travel guide also lists a Busay Falls near Pintuyan, so there may be two falls with this name. Confirm before publishing.

name: Tangkaan Beach
address: Brgy. Tangkaan, Padre Burgos, Southern Leyte
description: White coral-sand beach with rock formations and a view across to Limasawa; good for families and a frequent dive and snorkel spot. Bring your own food.

name: Padre Burgos Castle Resort
address: Brgy. Tangkaan, Padre Burgos, Southern Leyte
description: Castle-style resort above a private beach in Tangkaan, with a dive shop and restaurant.

name: Likay-Likay Beach
description: Beach in Padre Burgos known for fishing and snorkeling.

name: Bukana (Buenavista)
address: Brgy. Buenavista, Padre Burgos, Southern Leyte
description: Small calm pool of water in Buenavista that serves as a home for many fish.

name: Tangka-an Point Dive Site
address: Brgy. Tangkaan, Padre Burgos, Southern Leyte
description: Marine protected area near the mouth of Sogod Bay with a soft-coral slope to about 27 m, barrel sponges and gorgonian fans; frogfish, turtles and the occasional whale shark.

name: Adrien's Cove and Gunter's Wall
address: Brgy. Tangkaan, Padre Burgos, Southern Leyte
description: Adrien's Cove lies on the east side of Tangka-an Point, part of the largest marine sanctuary in Southern Leyte; Gunter's Wall is a reef wall that starts at the cove and runs south.
note: Sources disagree: one dive guide puts Adrian's Cove on Limasawa, another on Tangka-an Point (Padre Burgos).

name: Santa Sofia Dive Site
description: Marine protected area just south of Padre Burgos: a gentle hard-coral slope down to a sandy bottom around 25 m, good for macro (nudibranchs, pygmy seahorses, scorpionfish) and hawksbill turtles.

name: Padre Burgos Pier Dive Sites
description: A 150 m working pier in the middle of the town shoreline, regarded as one of the best night dives in the Philippines. Muck diving in about 5 m of water with octopus, flatworms, nudibranchs, seahorses, stargazers and lionfish. Divers have the pier on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays; anglers use it on other days.

name: Napantao Marine Sanctuary
address: Brgy. Napantao, San Francisco, Southern Leyte
description: First designated marine protected area in Sogod Bay, set up with Coral Cay Conservation in 2002. A wall across the bay from Padre Burgos, split into north and south sections, with anthias, gorgonian fans, frogfish and nudibranchs; whale sharks are sometimes seen.

name: Son-ok (Sun-ok) Marine Sanctuary
description: Marine sanctuary at Son-ok Point on Panaon Island, with the most documented whale shark encounters in Southern Leyte (roughly October to April).

name: Panaon Island Coast
description: Island at the southern end of the province with pebble and coral beaches and clear water. Covers several towns, so the pin is only the San Francisco town center.
note: Regional area; use a specific beach pin when you have one.

name: National Shrine of the First Mass in the Philippines
description: Shrine marking the traditional site of the first Catholic Mass in the Philippines on March 31, 1521. Main pilgrimage site of the island.

name: First Cross Monument
description: Monument on Limasawa linked to the first Mass site.

name: Dakdak Beach
description: Cream-sand beach in Lugsongan about 10 minutes from Triana port, with air-conditioned rooms, open-air huts and a small restaurant (Dak-dak Beach Resort).

name: Gamot Beach
description: Beach in Cabulihan on Limasawa.

name: Limasawa Island Lagoon
address: Brgy. San Agustin, Limasawa, Southern Leyte
description: Lagoon resort about 30 minutes from the town proper with kayaking, boating, snorkeling and cliff jumping.

name: Limasawa Caves
description: Caves in San Agustin and Magallanes that can be explored on the island.

name: Molopolo Fish and Bird Sanctuary
description: Molopolo-Sta. Cruz Marine Park in Macrohon: feed the fish a few meters from the highway, boat through the mangroves, and see a sea turtle hatching ground. Won third prize for Best Marine Protected Area in the Philippines in 2013.
note: Official site confirms Macrohon (Brgys. Molopolo and Sta. Cruz).

name: Cambaro Cave
description: Billed as the caving capital of Southern Leyte: more than 100 caves with speleothems, rock formations, cave corals and tunnels, reached after a mountain trek.

name: Kuting Reef Resort
description: Beach resort with a private beach and a reef right in front.

name: Florencia Island
description: Small island listed among Macrohon eco-tourism attractions.

name: Banahaw Cold Spring
address: Brgy. San Joaquin, Macrohon, Southern Leyte
description: Man-made pool filled with cold spring water, about 13 km (20-30 minutes) from Maasin. Day cottages, overnight rooms, barbecue area and a restaurant on site.

name: Seven Falls
address: Brgy. San Roque, Macrohon, Southern Leyte
description: Series of waterfalls about a 10-minute walk from the national road.

name: Baluarte Watchtower Ruins (Caaga)
description: Ruins of an 18th-century watchtower (baluarte) south of the poblacion, one of two near the church.

name: Baluarte Watchtower Ruins (Abgao)
description: Second ruined watchtower, north of the poblacion, with inscriptions on its stone walls.

name: Agas-Agas Bridge
description: Prestressed concrete bridge on the Pan-Philippine Highway, about 350 m long and 89 m high, with a tourist pavilion, parking and food kiosks.

name: Zipline Leyte (Agas-Agas Zipline)
description: Twin zipline opened in April 2011, about 880 m long, gliding diagonally above the bridge and gorge.
note: Pin is the bridge; the zipline stations are close by.

name: Magsuhot Park
description: Forested park of about 500 hectares, 3 km from the Phil-Japan Highway at Agas-Agas Bridge, with 20 m falls dropping into one basin; Lum-an and Mahayhay Falls (about 60 m) lie roughly 12 km farther.

name: Sogod Bay
description: Long central bay of the province, the main dive and snorkel area, with whale sharks between roughly October and April.
note: Pin is the approximate bay center used in your RightNowStrip, not an official point.

name: Kagut-an Falls
description: Falls about 1 km from the national highway, paired with a second falls close by.

name: Kagut-an Dako Dos Falls
description: Companion falls in the same barangay, singled out in the municipal tourism write-up.

name: Kagut-an Gamay Falls
description: Smaller falls in the same barangay.

name: Sitio Kawayan Falls
description: Roughly 10 m falls about 1 km from the Mercedes barangay road.

name: Tubod Falls and Cave
description: Distinctively shaped falls with a cave on the opposite side, joining the Lanang River downstream.

name: Silago Beach
description: Fine brown-sand beach about 1 km long at the Lanang River mouth. The town is promoted as the surfing capital of Southern Leyte.

name: Hindag-an Falls and Forest Park
address: Brgy. Hindag-an, Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte
description: Cascading falls feeding man-made pools with built-in waterslides, with cottages, restrooms and barbecue areas; about 30 minutes from Saint Bernard town proper. No overnight stay.

name: Uwan-Uwanan Falls
description: Gorge adventure of about a two-hour trek with rappelling and bamboo ladders along cascades.

name: Bosai Falls
description: Cold cascading falls in Barangay Ilag.

name: El Paraiso Beach
description: Beach with house rentals; reservation needed.

name: Alejos Falls
description: Falls in cold bluish water, about 30 minutes by vehicle from the main road to Dao, then a 35-minute trek.

name: San Pedro Island
description: Island off Hinunangan with a white pebble beach, clear water, coral and views of sunrise and sunset; limited cottages, some resorts.

name: San Pablo Island
description: Neighbor of San Pedro island with white-sand beach and coral gardens.

name: Mount Nacolod
description: Prominent peak in Hinunangan, about 948 m according to Wikipedia.

name: Lake Danao
description: Crater lake near the top of Mt. Cabalian, on the border of San Juan and Anahawan, reached by a demanding forest trek with blue-green volcanic water as the reward.
note: Lake straddles San Juan and Anahawan; pin is San Juan town.

name: Mama Mary Shrine (Jalleca Hills)
address: Brgy. Mantahan, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: 36 ft Our Lady of the Assumption statue on a hilltop about 310 ft above sea level, reached by more than 300 steps.

name: Sto. Niño Shrine on Pagatpat Islet
address: Brgy. Mahayahay, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Shrine on a small islet, a short pumpboat ride from Sitio Pangpang after a 10-minute walk from the national highway.

name: Abiera's Museum
address: Brgy. Tunga-Tunga, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Private museum of local collector Salvador "Boy" Abiera: ancient artifacts, fossils, a burial jar, Chinese porcelain, old weapons, shells and preserved wildlife.

name: Hapitan Beach and Mangrove Eco-Forest Park
address: Brgy. Manhilo, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Summer hangout with both sea and fresh water, 10-15 minutes by road from Maasin.

name: Maasin City Zoo (Danao Forest Park)
address: Brgy. Malapoc Norte, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Animal park inside Camp Danao, about 30 minutes from the city center, with lions, tigers, crocodiles, tarsiers, camels and other animals.
note: Official page puts it in Sitio Danao, Malapoc Norte.

name: Santo Niño Parish Church (Malitbog)
description: Parish church noted for its local Filipino-style facade and a ceiling painted with religious motifs.

name: Calag-itan Fish Sanctuary
description: Community-run marine protected area where visitors feed fish and snorkel; reachable by road by any vehicle or by public van or bus.

name: Hinunangan Golden Sand Beach
description: About 6 km of powdery golden sand with the best view of the twin islands San Pedro and San Pablo.

name: Southern Leyte Divers Resort
address: Brgy. San Roque, Macrohon, Southern Leyte
description: Dive resort with sea views in San Roque.

name: Flordeliz Beach Resort
description: White-sand beach resort with grilling stations and nipa-and-bamboo cottages.

name: Tagbak Marine Park
description: Marine park with clear water and healthy reefs, reached by motorboat.

name: Silago Surfing Camp
description: Promoted as the surfing capital of Southern Leyte, good for beginners and intermediates and for backpackers who camp.

name: Silago Tropical Rainforest
description: Forest reserve with rich flora and fauna; a tree-top canopy walk is planned as the first facility.

name: Pelada Rock (Batong Dako)
description: Large rock just offshore between Barangays Laguma and Salvacion, used as a camp by the Japanese army in WWII and now home to nesting birds.

name: Mahaba Beach
description: Clear, cool-water beach with rock formations at the side and colorful fish a few meters out.

name: Sogod Bay Scuba Resort
description: Dive resort a short distance from Padre Burgos town center, with a restaurant and water sports.

name: Evashore Beach Resort
description: Beachfront resort on Limasawa Island.

name: Totoy Peak
description: Viewpoint about 30 minutes from Triana, known for sunsets and views of the sea and nearby barangays.

name: Magellan's Cross Replica (450 steps)
description: Replica of the cross on a hilltop beside the First Mass Shrine, reached by a 450-step climb with rest stops and a good view.

name: Limasawa Island Dive Sites
description: Walls, drop-offs and fan corals with sites for beginners too; the official site groups them with Padre Burgos dives.

name: Naputjukan Underwater Cave
description: Sea cave of roughly 200 sq m with a white-sand beach, stalagmites and arch-like stalactites, entered by banca through a sea-facing opening.

name: Napandong Rock Formation
description: Canopy-like rock formation along a cliff side.

name: Catbawan Waterfalls Safari
description: Seven different waterfalls within less than an hour, with green scenery and challenging trails.

name: Guinsaugon Eco-adventure National Park (Ground Zero)
address: Brgy. Guinsaugon, Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte
description: Memorial site of the February 2006 landslide that buried the village; declared a national park, visitors light candles and trek, and the last stretch is on foot.

name: Bosong-bosong Spring and Tinugpahan Falls
address: Brgy. Mapgap, Tomas Oppus, Southern Leyte
description: Newly developed spring grove, with a two-hour river trek to Tinugpahan Falls and its arena-like pool.

name: Mainit Hot Spring
description: Sulfuric hot spring on Mt. Cabalian, about 63.4-63.9 C, believed to be medicinal.

name: Mt. Cabalian Trail
description: Forest trail to Lake Danao on the volcanic Mt. Cabalian, shared with San Juan.
note: Mountain spans Anahawan and San Juan.

name: San Francisco Javier Pilgrims Center
address: Brgy. Hanginan, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Hilltop shrine reached by a trek of two hours or more from Brgy. Isagani; the Hanginan trail is said to be the highest point of the city and was a Spanish-era watchpoint.

name: Sagpun Falls
address: Brgy. Ibarra, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Waterfall in Barangay Ibarra.

name: Tunga-Tunga Beach
address: Brgy. Tunga-Tunga, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: About 1,000 sq m of white sand, listed as one of the most popular beaches in Maasin.

name: Little Denmark Beach
address: Brgy. Bilibol, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Beach at Sitio Panas, Barangay Bilibol.

name: Mercado Beach
address: Brgy. Ibarra, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Beach in Barangay Ibarra.

name: Talisay Beach
address: Brgy. Ibarra, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Beach in Barangay Ibarra.

name: Dakong Bato sa Pugaling
address: Brgy. Isagani, Maasin City, Southern Leyte
description: Beach and rock spot in Barangay Isagani.

name: Bitu-on Beach
address: Brgy. San Roque, Liloan, Southern Leyte
description: Beach in Barangay San Roque, Liloan, listed in older provincial notes and on Wikivoyage.
note: Older blog source; confirm the barangay.

name: Demoloc Caves
description: Caves in Malitbog that appear among the top places listed for the town.
note: Only one source and no detail; confirm barangay and access.

name: Lum-an Falls
description: Falls of about 60 m, around 12 km beyond Magsuhot Park according to the provincial tourism page.

name: Mahayhay Falls
description: Falls of about 60 m near Lum-an Falls; Wanderlog lists it as one of Sogod's best-known places.

name: Talisay (Hinunangan)
description: Named alongside Tahusan and the twin islands as a tourist place of Hinunangan.
note: Barangay assumed from the name; confirm what visitors do there.

name: Ilijan Point
description: Point near the Napantao sanctuary where snorkelers and divers see many fish and sea turtles.

name: Sogod Bay Scuba Resort House Reef (Max Climax)
description: Wall dive in front of the resort, from about 8 m down to 45 m, with hard and soft corals, sweetlips, snappers, crabs and shrimps; strong currents are possible and the shore entry is rough.

name: Little Lembeh Dive Site
description: Muck-diving site marked by stilt huts, about 30 minutes by boat north of Padre Burgos, with pipefish, seahorses, pegasus fish and nudibranchs over black sand.
note: Exact town not stated; pin is Padre Burgos as the reference point.

name: Zack's Cove (Limasawa)
description: One of Limasawa's two main dive sites with Adrian's Cove, known for reefscapes and a good chance of whale sharks.

name: Dan-an Falls
description: Waterfall mentioned by travelers around Pintuyan on Panaon Island.

name: Tag-linaw Falls
description: Falls shown in a Pintuyan travel guide.
note: Name read from a photo caption; confirm spelling and location.

name: Caningag Viewpoint
description: Scenic viewpoint around Pintuyan.
note: Barangay assumed from the name; confirm.

name: Son-ok Peak
description: Hill and peak near the Son-ok marine sanctuary, mentioned by travelers around Pintuyan.

name: Luman Falls
description: Falls listed among the best-known sights around San Juan.
note: One blog also places Lum-an Falls near Sogod; these may be different falls.

name: San Juan Children's Park
description: Town park listed among San Juan's sights.
